land.text: Avanti with Vatsa: 'He conquered Avanti kingdom by defeating Nandivardhana or Avantivardhana, the last king of Pradyota dynasty'

successors.note: Shishunaga reigned c. 413-395 BCE; Cliopatria's Shaishunaga row begins -404. The land is the corrected shape (Malwa, Mahishmati, Vatsa), far larger than Cliopatria's Avanti core.

capitals.name: Ujjayini (Ujjain)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Ujjayini (northern Avanti)'; 'the southern part had its centre at Mahishmati' (Maheshwar on the Narmada, 22.18N 75.58E).

correction.text: Avanti, 'roughly corresponding to the present-day Malwa region', divided by the Vindhyas into a northern part 'drained by the Sipra river' around Ujjayini and a southern part 'drained by the Narmada' with 'its centre at Mahishmati'

keyframe_review.note: The 5,104 km2 shape is the Ujjain core alone (centroid 75.78E 23.24N); the page gives the whole Malwa and a southern half on the Narmada at Mahishmati (Maheshwar, 22.18N 75.58E), which the shape omits. The gazetteer's Malwa resolves to about 155,000 km2, thirty times the shape; the Mahajanapadas page's 'Malwa, Nimar and adjoining parts of Madhya Pradesh' agrees. The infobox gives no area. Maheshwar is not in the gazetteer.

correction.text: Avanti (Malwa and the Narmada country at Mahishmati) with Vatsa: 'Vatsa was already part of Avanti' under Palaka (Kathasaritsagara)

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria repeats the shape from -450, the year after its Vatsa row ends (-451); the page has Vatsa 'already part of Avanti under Palaka' (undated), so the Vatsa shape is added from -450 at confidence 1. The Shishunaga page has Shishunaga conquer 'Kosala and Vatsa' separately c. 413-395 BCE, which may mean Vatsa had slipped from Avanti again.

region.text: Avanti, 'roughly corresponding to the present-day Malwa region', divided by the Vindhyas into a northern part 'drained by the Sipra river' around Ujjayini and a southern part 'drained by the Narmada' with 'its centre at Mahishmati'

ledger.note: c. 600 BCE: Avanti, ruled from Ujjayini with a southern seat at Mahishmati. Infobox 'Established c. 700 BCE', 'Capital Ujjayini'; 'the Haihayas were the earliest rulers of Avanti' from Mahishmati, and the last Vitihotra king Ripunjaya was overthrown by his minister Pulika, 'who put his son Pradyota on the throne' (Pradyota 'a contemporary of Gautama Buddha', undated). -600 is the Mahajanapada convention; the Haihaya Avanti before it is left to batch sa-01-x.

region.text: Vatsa, the kingdom of Kausambi: 'Vatsa was already part of Avanti' under Palaka

ledger.note: c. 450 BCE (undated): Vatsa passes under Avanti. 'Per the Kathasaritsagara, Vatsa was already part of Avanti under Palaka', Pradyota's successor, who 'ascended on the day of passing away of Mahavira' (Jain accounts); the year is Cliopatria's end of the Vatsa row (-451). The Vatsa agent (sa-01) should carry the matching loss or correct the date.

region.text: Avanti (Malwa and the Narmada country at Mahishmati) with Vatsa: 'Vatsa was already part of Avanti' under Palaka (Kathasaritsagara)

ledger.note: c. 405 BCE: Shishunaga of Magadha destroys the Pradyota dynasty and takes Avanti. 'He conquered Avanti kingdom by defeating Nandivardhana or Avantivardhana, the last king of Pradyota dynasty'; 'He destroyed Pradyota dynasty of Avanti and conquered kingdoms of Kosala and Vatsa'; reign 'c. 413 - c. 395 BCE'. The year is Cliopatria's (its Shaishunaga row begins -404); the pages give no year within the reign. Avanti page: 'He was defeated by Shishunaga, the king of Magadha'; 'Under the Nandas it became the Avantirattha, the western province'.

wars.name: Avanti-Vatsa war of Pradyota and Udayana
wars.outcome: Pradyota 'captured Vatsa king Udayana, then married his daughter Vasavadatta to Udayana'; no land changed hands then, but under Palaka 'Vatsa was already part of Avanti' (ledger -450).
wars.note: Undated; Pradyota was 'a contemporary of Gautama Buddha'. The years run to the ledger's -450 gain.

wars.name: Pradyota's threat to Magadha
wars.outcome: No campaign recorded: Ajatashatru fortified Rajagriha 'to protect it from an invasion led by Pradyota' (Majjhima Nikaya).
wars.note: Undated; Ajatashatru's Magadha is Cliopatria's Haryanka row (-500..-405).

wars.name: Pradyota's war with Pushkarasarin of Takshashila
wars.outcome: 'Pradyota waged war on Pushkarasarin, king of Takshashila'; the Gandhara (kingdom) page has Pukkusati 'successful in this struggle with Pradyota'. No land changed hands.
wars.note: Undated; Pukkusati is dated c. 550 BCE on the Gandhara (kingdom) page and Gandhara west of the Indus fell to Cyrus c. 535 BCE.

wars.name: Shishunaga's conquest of Avanti

zones.text: Avanti, the Malwa country around Ujjayini

wars.outcome: Magadhan victory: the Pradyota dynasty destroyed and Avanti taken; 'The Magadhan victory must have been helped by the revolution that placed Aryaka on the throne of Ujjayini'.
wars.note: The years are Shishunaga's accession (c. 413 BCE) to Cliopatria's end of the Avanti row (-405); no page dates the campaign within the reign.

certainty.note: The Vindhyas divide the two halves; no outer frontier is recorded, and the Vatsa addition from -450 rests on one undated sentence.

sources.title: Avanti (region)
sources.note: Identity, infobox (c. 700 - c. 300 BCE, Ujjayini, Mahishmati), Malwa, the Haihayas and Pradyotas, Udayana, Palaka and Vatsa, Shishunaga's defeat of the last Pradyota, the Nanda province.

sources.title: Shishunaga
sources.note: Reign c. 413-395 BCE, the conquest of Avanti ('defeating Nandivardhana or Avantivardhana'), Kosala and Vatsa.

sources.title: Mahajanapadas
sources.note: Overview of the sixteen states ('from the sixth to fourth centuries BCE'), the Mahajanapada convention behind every -600 start, and the per-state location notes; shared by the five janapada dossiers of batch sa-01-a.

notes: Both Cliopatria shapes are the Ujjain core only and are enlarged to the page's Malwa with the Narmada country at Mahishmati (adjust). The -450 keyframe is read as the absorption of Vatsa (Kathasaritsagara, undated; confidence 1) because Cliopatria ends Vatsa in -451 and restarts Avanti in -450; the Vatsa agent should confirm or move it. The end (-405) is Cliopatria's year inside Shishunaga's reign c. 413-395 BCE; the infobox's 'c. 300 BCE' end describes Avanti as a Magadhan province and is not drawn. Pradyota's accession (Pulika's coup over Ripunjaya) and Aryaka's revolt against Palaka are undated and left out of the ledger. Gazetteer names lacking: place Maheshwar (Mahishmati, on the Narmada, 22.18N 75.58E); 'Nimar' (the Narmada valley region named by the Mahajanapadas page) is also absent.
